changelog: Settings persistence, diagnosed per the ticket before any fix: traced the complete round trip end to end against a realistic simulated backend (a real in-memory 'server' the test suite writes to and reads back from, not just trusting the client's own optimistic state) -- confirmed every individual settings-panel field change fires update_backtest_drawing with a payload that includes both points and the full settings object; confirmed BacktestDrawingController::update() writes both columns unconditionally once ownership is verified; confirmed reopening the same drawing without any reload shows the saved values; and confirmed a full reload from the server (simulating a page refresh or reopening the session) restores both settings AND geometry correctly. Also stress-tested up to 43 rapid overlapping save requests (simulating fast slider dragging) under artificial network jitter across repeated runs and could not reproduce data loss in this environment.

Could not force a reproduction, but did find one genuine, real correctness gap regardless: each settings field saves independently and concurrently (colour pickers and the opacity slider also fire on live drag, not just on release), with no ordering guarantee between overlapping requests -- on a real network, an earlier edit's request arriving at the server after a later one's would let its older payload win the final write, silently reverting the more recent change. This is exactly the failure shape described (edits appearing to vanish) even though the local test harness's near-instant request/response cycle didn't expose it. Closed the gap regardless: saves for a given drawing are now serialized (btUpdateDrawing queues onto a per-drawing promise chain), each one reading the truly-current state at send time rather than at the moment it was queued -- a burst of rapid edits now collapses into however many requests actually fire, each one carrying the complete, correct, current state. If settings loss still occurs after this release, it did not reproduce through any client/server round trip or concurrency scenario tested here -- exact repro steps (browser, whether a real reload happened, how many fields were changed and how quickly) would help narrow it further.

Fib labels were rendering ON TOP of their own level line (e.g. '0.618 — 6799.39' printed across the line itself) -- the label was anchored right at the line's own end and aligned so its text grew back over the line rather than away from it. Flipped the alignment: the label now starts just past the line's end on the chosen side (a small gap) and grows away from it, clamped so it never crosses into the price-scale panel even when the line itself is extended. Verified in-browser on both Label Side settings: every label's near edge sits clear of the line by the gap, and with extend-right on, labels still stay inside the plot area rather than following the line to the canvas edge.
release_notes: No schema changes in this release -- nothing to migrate. Per instruction, nothing was deployed as part of this turn.
